digest.top_line: POSEIDON (6057 pts): adding HT to postop RT gave no OS benefit (HR 0·87, 0·76–1·01), with signal confined to pre-PORT PSA >0·5.
digest.tldr: Prostate carried the day: POSEIDON says salvage RT alone suffices below PSA 0·5, and GÖTEBORG-1's 25-yr AS data shows 94% PC-specific survival but 68% failure-free at 22 yr. RT technique gains elsewhere: immune-sparing lung SBRT cut G3 lymphopenia to 0%, and MIBC SIB boost dropped 2y invasive local recurrence 27·5% → 5·5%.

sites.intro: First randomised test of planning to spare circulating lymphocytes rather than only meeting standard OAR constraints.

studies.name: NCT04273893 (Immune-Cell-Sparing SBRT)
studies.tldr: Overall ALC-reduction improvement 13.4% (95% CI 2.8-24.0), p=0.01, favoring immune-organ-sparing lung SBRT planning.

details.text: 🔍 Randomized phase II, N=51 (25 optimized / 26 standard), single institution, 2020-2023, unmasked, stratified by tumor location

details: 🔍 Both arms met RTOG 0813/0915 constraints; optimized arm additionally minimized dose to heart, great vessels, lymph-node-stations, thoracic-spine

details.text: 🔍 SBRT 45-60 Gy in 5 fx (BED 85.5-132 Gy) via IMRT/VMAT; ITV from 4DCT, PTV margin 5 mm radial / 8 mm sup-inf
📊 Average % reduction in optimized vs standard plans (integral dose, V5, V10)
📐 ALC % change from baseline by timepoint (model-estimated)
📊 Central tumors (n=15) gained most: overall ALC-reduction improvement 29.5% (95% CI 10.1-48.9), p=0.004
📊 Peripheral PTV >20cc (n=18): improvement 13.5%, 95% CI -3.8 to 20.9, p=0.124; peripheral PTV <20cc showed no difference

details: 📊 G3 lymphopenia 15.4% standard vs 0% optimized (risk difference -15.4%, 95% CI -29.2 to -1.5, p=0.04)
📊 LN-stations V5 below vs above 35.4cc median: two-year OS 91.8% vs 57.5%, p=0.02
⚠️ OS/EFS were unplanned subgroup analyses, not powered; all-patient OS p=0.23, EFS p=0.27
⚠️ Baseline imbalance favors caution: more central tumors in optimized arm (36.0% vs 23.1%), more treatment-naive in standard arm (88.5% vs 64.0%)
⚠️ ALC is a surrogate; no immune-function or tumor-control readout ties the spared lymphocytes to the survival trend
🔗 Prior prospective RT+IO data cited by the authors linked lower post-RT ALC to worse PFS (p=.009) and OS (p=.026); this is the first trial to spare prospectively

verdict.rationale: Preprint, not peer-reviewed. Single-institution randomized phase II, N=51, surrogate primary (ALC); survival analyses unplanned and underpowered. Confirmatory multi-institutional trial named by authors.
verdict.audience: Early-stage NSCLC (cT1-T2 N0), medically inoperable or declined surgery, pre-RT…

studies.significance: The planning ask is concrete: add heart, great vessels, thoracic spine and lymph-node stations as low-dose OARs and drive V5/V10 down (thoracic spine V5 fell 87%, lymph-node stations 58%) without breaching RTOG 0813/0915. Benefit concentrated in central tumors and peripheral PTV >20cc; peripheral PTV <20cc gained nothing, so the effort is worth spending selectively.
studies.monday_clinic: For a medically inoperable early-stage NSCLC pt with a central or larger (>20cc PTV) tumor, this supports adding immune-rich low-dose OAR objectives to an otherwise standard 5-fraction plan; it does not apply to small peripheral tumors, where the two planning approaches were indistinguishable.

primary_endpoint.name: ALC depletion vs standard planning (all timepoints)

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Randomized **phase II**, single institution, 2020-2023. 55 enrolled, 4 withdrew/ineligible, **51 randomized 1:1** (25 optimized, 26 standard), stratified by tumor location, **treatment assignment not masked**. Database lock June 30 2024.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Early-stage NSCLC (AJCC v8), pathologic or imaging-confirmed, **unable or unwilling to undergo surgery**; ECOG 0-2; pre-RT **ALC >0.5 x10⁹/L**. Recurrent previously treated NSCLC eligible. Median age 74 both arms; cT1 in 25/25 optimized and 23/26 standard.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **SBRT 45-60 Gy in 5 fractions** (BED 85.5-132 Gy), IMRT or VMAT, 6X-FFF, daily CBCT. Both arms met **RTOG 0813/0915** criteria; the optimized arm additionally minimized dose to heart, great vessels, **lymph-node stations** (Chapet atlas, down to 40 cGy/fx) and thoracic spine. PTV = ITV + **5 mm radial, 8 mm sup-inf**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary:** less in vivo lymphocyte depletion with optimized planning at end-of-treatment, 4 weeks and 6 months, plus safety/toxicity comparison. OS and EFS were **unplanned exploratory** Kaplan-Meier analyses.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: G3+ AEs: **2 optimized** (lung infection) vs **4 standard** (dyspnea, hypoxia, lung infection); all recovered. G2 events in 6 (24%) optimized vs 9 (35%) standard. **No G2+ pneumonitis and no G4+ toxicity** in either arm, so the added low-dose objectives cost nothing in toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents medically inoperable early-stage NSCLC treated with 5-fraction SBRT, particularly central or PTV >20cc tumors. Does not represent locally advanced disease, conventionally fractionated thoracic RT, or concurrent chemo/immunotherapy, all of which were exclusions.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Randomization left the arms unbalanced on the two variables that most move the survival read: central tumors 36.0% vs 23.1% and treatment-naive 88.5% standard vs 64.0% optimized, so the OS trend is reported only in the treatment-naive subset. Static organ dose is a surrogate for dose to circulating lymphocytes, and the authors note the correlation coefficients are small.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The mechanism argument is dosimetric, not immunologic: heart and great-vessel V5/V10 stand in for blood transiting a high-flux volume, thoracic spine and nodes for resident lymphocytes. Multiple immune OARs compete for the same dose reduction (Fig 2), so the authors argue for a cumulative per-plan immune-kill objective rather than per-organ constraints.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This is a planning-objective change, not a prescription change: same 45-60 Gy in 5 fx meeting RTOG 0813/0915, plus heart, great vessels, thoracic spine and lymph-node stations contoured as low-dose OARs. Achieved V5 reductions were 87% (spine) and 58% (nodes) with no increase in G3+ toxicity, and the gain was confined to central and PTV >20cc cases.

open_questions: Does immune sparing translate to OS or EFS benefit in a powered trial?
Which immune-rich OAR carries the dominant RIIS contribution?
Does immune-sparing planning add to SBRT plus immunotherapy?

sites.intro: First international consensus contouring guideline for RCC SABR, CT-only by design.

studies.name: IROCK RCC Contouring Guidelines
studies.tldr: First international consensus contouring guideline for RCC SABR; 16 experts, median DSC 0.85 across 4 scenarios.
details: 🔍 16 RCC SABR experts (US, Canada, Australia, Netherlands, India), all with ≥10 prior RCC SABR cases; 14/16 treated ≥10 in the prior 12mo
🔍 4 CT-only cases: >10cm tumor + IVC thrombus, central tumor abutting hilum, post-nephrectomy local recurrence, post-RFA residual
🔍 STAPLE 95% consensus contour per case; refined over 2 online meetings (May, June 2024); statements revised to 100% agreement

details.text: 📊 Contour agreement vs consensus by case (median, IQR)
📐 Overall metrics and ANOVA
subdetails: DSC, MDA, HD all differed by case (P<.05); by participant only MDA differed (P=.03), DSC P=.07, HD P=.45

details.text: 📐 Target volume rules per scenario
subdetails: iGTV includes primary tumor + entire tumor thrombus; bland thrombus excluded
iGTV includes gross tumor recurrence + the entire post-RFA ablation cavity
Surgical clips not involved with tumor can be left out of the iGTV
No margin for microscopic spread; most common PTV margin was uniform 5mm on iGTV

details: 📐 5mm PTV margin assumes supine vacuum-cushion immobilization, 4D-CT sim, IV contrast, daily CBCT; varies with MRI-sim or adaptive workflows
📐 Ipsilateral renal parenchyma = whole ipsilateral kidney minus iGTV, renal pelvis, renal vasculature, proximal ureter
⚠️ Renal hilum explicitly NOT a dose-limiting OAR: optional contour only, since constraining it may push dose into remaining parenchyma
📐 OAR constraints take priority over target coverage; heterogeneous PTV dose with steep gradient is the stated tradeoff, hotspot inside the iGTV
💊 Bowel/stomach mitigation: NPO for hours pre-sim and pre-treatment, simethicone or alpha-galactosidase, bowel prep, PRVs, adaptive RT if available
🔗 Suggested 1/3/5-fraction dose objectives and OAR constraints (Table 2) are drawn from FASTRACK-II and AQuOS-II (NCT05023265) protocols, not derived here
⚠️ CT-only exercise by design; participants themselves asked for MRI, and the authors concede MRI availability would likely have narrowed the variation
⚠️ No recontouring after the 2 consensus meetings, so the post-guideline agreement gain is asserted, not measured
⚠️ Widest spread was Case 1 (superior extent of IVC thrombus, HD median 64.60mm) and Case 4 (how much RFA cavity to include, DSC 0.75)

verdict.rationale: Expert consensus contouring atlas, not an outcome study; DSC/MDA/HD measure inter-observer agreement, not efficacy. Recommendations unvalidated prospectively.
verdict.audience: Localized RCC considered for SABR, incl. IVC thrombus, central, post-RN or…

studies.significance: The two decision-carrying rules are the ones most likely to be got wrong: cover the entire ablation cavity, not just the residual nodule, and the entire tumor thrombus while excluding bland thrombus. Renal hilum is deliberately not a dose-limiting OAR. Case 4 DSC 0.75 and Case 1 HD median 64.60mm mark where experts still disagree.
studies.monday_clinic: For a localized RCC patient being planned for SABR with an IVC thrombus or a post-RFA cavity, this defines the iGTV extent and the 5mm PTV margin under 4D-CT plus daily CBCT; it does not speak to whether SABR or nephrectomy is the right choice.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: International consensus contouring exercise under IROCK, panel convened at **ASTRO 2023**. Each participant contoured the **iGTV** on 4 CT-only cases plus 2 investigational renal substructures; a **STAPLE** algorithm generated the 95% consensus contour, refined over **2 online meetings** (May and June 2024).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **16 radiation oncologists** from the US, Canada, Australia, the Netherlands and India. Sole inclusion criterion was **≥10 prior RCC SABR cases**; 14 of 16 had treated ≥10 in the preceding 12 months. All 16 contoured targets for every case; **12 and 13** contoured the renal cortex and renal hilum respectively, the rest judging those structures not relevant.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **No margin for microscopic spread**: iGTV = ITV, and the most common recommended PTV expansion was a **uniform 5 mm**, premised on supine vacuum-cushion immobilization, 4D-CT sim, IV contrast and daily CBCT. Participants used **1, 3, or 5 fractions**; suggested coverage objectives and OAR constraints (Table 2) are adapted from **FASTRACK-II** and **AQuOS-II** rather than generated by this panel.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Agreement metrics only: **DSC**, **Mean Distance to Agreement** and **Hausdorff Distance** of each participant's contour against the consensus contour, with a 2-way ANOVA across cases and participants. There is **no clinical endpoint** here.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Median DSC **0.85** (range 0.40-0.95), median MDA **2.17 mm**, median HD **9.00 mm**; DSC exceeded **0.70** in every case. Agreement tracked case complexity, not operator: DSC and HD differed significantly by case but not by participant (**P=.07** and **P=.45**), while MDA differed by participant (**P=.03**).

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The substantive novelty is renal substructure handling. Ipsilateral renal parenchyma is defined as the whole ipsilateral kidney **minus iGTV, renal pelvis, renal vasculature and proximal ureter**, and the hilum is explicitly **not a dose-limiting OAR**, on the reasoning that sparing it would displace dose into the remaining functional parenchyma. Where OAR constraints and target coverage conflict, **constraints win**, accepting heterogeneous target dose with a steep gradient.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents localized RCC planned for SABR, including large tumors with IVC tumor thrombus, central tumors abutting the hilum, post-nephrectomy local recurrence and post-RFA residual disease. Does not represent metastatic RCC, non-RCC renal histologies, or centers planning on MRI, since only CT was distributed.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: CT-only distribution likely inflated the measured variance, and participants were never asked to recontour after the consensus meetings, so the claimed improvement is untested. Implementation depends on multidisciplinary access to urology, IR and nephrology plus advanced planning technology, and the recommendations have not been validated in a prospective trial.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Two rules carry the planning decision: the entire post-RFA ablation cavity goes in the iGTV, not just the residual nodule, and the whole tumor thrombus goes in while bland thrombus stays out. The 5mm PTV margin is conditional on 4D-CT and daily CBCT. Renal hilum stays an optional contour, never a dose-limiting OAR.

open_questions: Does renal hilum dose actually drive stenosis or ureteric stricture?
Would MRI-based simulation reduce the Case 1 and Case 4 variance?
Do these contours improve outcomes prospectively?

sites.intro: Retrospective SIB dose escalation in TMT, with a local-control gain that does not carry to OS or MFS.

studies.name: Dose-Escalated RT for MIBC
studies.tldr: 2y invasive local recurrence 5.5% vs 27.5% with SIB dose escalation in TMT; SHR 0.20 (0.05-0.89), p=0.035, no OS or MFS difference.

details.text: 🔍 Multicentre retrospective, 3 centres, Mar 2015 to May 2025, N=107 (39 escalated / 68 standard), median f/u 23mo (range 3-104)
📐 Standard: 55Gy/20fx or 64Gy/32fx whole bladder. Escalation: SIB to 60Gy/20fx or 70Gy/32fx to the primary lesion

details: 📊 2y cumulative incidence invasive recurrence 5.5% (escalation) vs 27.5% (standard); crude 2/39 (5.1%) vs 16/68 (23.5%)
📐 Univariable Fine-Gray SHR 0.21 (0.05-0.94), p=0.04; multivariable adjusted for T stage SHR 0.20 (0.05-0.89), p=0.035

details.text: 📊 Escalation vs standard across endpoints

details: 📊 Only 1 of 2 invasive recurrences in the escalated cohort was inside the boost field; 14 of 16 standard-dose invasive recurrences were at the original tumour site

details.text: ⚠️ Escalation cohort was cleaner at baseline: single tumour focus 39 (100%) vs 44 (65%), hydronephrosis 4 (10%) vs 19 (28%), T3 3 (8%) vs 11 (16%)

details: ⚠️ Multivariable model adjusted for T stage only, so focality and hydronephrosis imbalance is unadjusted
⚠️ 3 standard-dose recurrences were presumed invasive on CT (no cystoscopy, comorbidity); all escalation-cohort recurrences were cystoscopy-confirmed
🔍 Chemo omitted in 51% for poor PS/comorbidity; absence of chemo carried worse OS (HR 2.83 [1.42, 5.63], p < 0.01 on MVA)
📊 Salvage cystectomy: 2 (2.9%) standard for invasive recurrence vs 1 (2.5%) escalation for BCG-refractory non-invasive disease; most invasive relapses were unfit for surgery

verdict.rationale: Retrospective 3-centre cohort, 39 escalated pts, 2 invasive events; escalation arm enriched for unifocal, non-hydronephrotic, T2 disease. Hypothesis-generating only.
verdict.audience: MIBC, T2-T3 N0-N1, TMT after TURBT, curative intent, incl. chemo-unfit

studies.significance: The signal is local, not systemic: invasive recurrence fell 27.5% to 5.5% at 2y with no MFS or OS shift, and 1 of the 2 escalated failures was still inside the boost. Deliverable as SIB 60Gy/20fx or 70Gy/32fx with daily CBCT, no G2+ GU/GI penalty (p=0.8, p=0.9), so it moves the boost-volume question, not patient selection for TMT.
studies.monday_clinic: In unifocal T2 MIBC going to TMT, including chemo-unfit pts, this supports discussing an SIB boost to the primary lesion as a local-control question; it does not extend to multifocal disease (0 of 39 escalated pts) or change the metastatic or survival calculus.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicentre **retrospective** analysis across three centres, March 2015 to May 2025, chosen to capture daily CBCT image guidance. **N=107** (39 dose-escalated, 68 standard), median follow-up **23 months** (range 3-104).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: MIBC after TURBT treated with RT with or without concurrent chemo, curative intent; **node-positive allowed** if non-metastatic, palliative-intent excluded. T2 in 92 (86%), node-positive 13, ECOG 2-3 in 54 (50%).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Standard cohort: **55Gy/20fx or 64Gy/32fx** to whole bladder. Escalation: **simultaneous integrated boost to 60Gy/20fx or 70Gy/32fx** to the primary lesion. Hypofractionation in 97 (91%); empty-bladder CT sim, planning MRI and FDG PET fused in selected pts; daily CBCT in all but one.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Concurrent chemo in 52 (49%): 22 (56%) escalation vs 30 (44%) standard. The **51% who had no chemo** were mostly excluded for poor performance status and comorbidity, not by protocol.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: 2-year local control for invasive and non-invasive disease, metastasis-free survival, overall survival, bladder preservation, and toxicity. Fine-Gray competing-risk analysis for recurrence; **no single registered primary endpoint** is stated.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Only invasive local control separated. Chemo omission (HR 2.83 [1.42, 5.63], p < 0.01) and hydronephrosis (HR 0.34 [0.16, 0.71], p < 0.01 for its absence) drove OS instead of dose.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: **G2+ GU** 17.9% escalation vs 22.1% standard (p=0.8); **G2+ GI** 5.1% vs 7.4% (p=0.9). Grade 3 toxicity in 2 pts (2.9%), **both in the standard arm**. No treatment stopped early for toxicity.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents unifocal T2-dominant MIBC without hydronephrosis treated by TMT with daily CBCT, including chemo-unfit pts. Does not represent multifocal disease, since 0 of 39 escalated pts had multiple foci and all 24 multifocal pts sat in the standard arm.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Two invasive events in the escalated arm carry the entire SHR, so the interval (0.05, 0.89) is fragile. Recurrence ascertainment differed by arm (3 standard-dose recurrences were imaging-presumed, all escalation recurrences cystoscopy-confirmed), and median 23-month follow-up under-counts late in-bladder failure.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The pattern-of-failure data is the more transferable read: 14 of 16 standard-dose invasive recurrences were at the original tumour site, which is the anatomic argument for boosting the GTV rather than escalating the whole bladder. Whether the 5.5% figure survives a prospective trial with balanced focality is the open question the authors themselves raise.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: SIB to 60Gy/20fx or 70Gy/32fx to the GTV, not whole-bladder escalation, is the deliverable technique here, and it cost nothing in G2+ GU or GI toxicity (p=0.8, p=0.9). With 14 of 16 standard-dose invasive failures at the original tumour site, this moves the boost-volume decision in TMT planning.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Half the cohort (51%) got no concurrent chemo, and chemo omission was the strongest OS covariate (HR 2.83 [1.42, 5.63], p < 0.01) while dose escalation moved neither MFS (p = 0.79) nor OS (p = 0.5). For a chemo-unfit MIBC pt, a boost addresses the bladder, not the systemic risk.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Salvage cystectomy rates were low in both arms (2.9% standard, 2.5% escalation), but the authors note most invasive relapses never reached surgery because pts were unfit at recurrence. In a comorbid TMT population, better up-front local control matters more than salvage availability.

open_questions: Does the invasive local control gain survive prospective randomisation?
Does the 5.5% figure hold beyond 23-month follow-up?

sites.intro: Two long-horizon datasets reframe when to add treatment: hormones to postop RT, and any treatment at all in screen-detected disease.

studies.name: GÖTEBORG-1
studies.tldr: PC-specific survival 94% at 25 yr on AS, but failure-free survival fell to 68% at 22 yr.

details.text: 🔍 488 screen-detected men on AS from the Göteborg-1 screening trial, 1995-2014; median f/u 18.0 yr (IQR 14.7-22.1)
🔍 Risk mix: 251 (51%) very-low, 129 (26%) low, 108 (22%) intermediate; high-risk excluded (n=6)
📊 KM outcomes for the whole cohort
📊 By risk group (PC-specific + OS at 24 yr; treatment-free at 19 yr)
📊 232 of 488 discontinued AS: 141 radical prostatectomy, 44 radiotherapy, 47 hormonal treatment
📊 81 failures: 14 PC deaths, 5 metastatic alive, 44 started HT, 18 PSA relapse post-curative treatment
📐 Multivariable Cox predictors of failure
🔗 Treatment-free survival 48% at 15 yr, vs 55% Toronto AS cohort (15 yr) and 49% PASS (10 yr)

details: 🔗 PC mortality below PIVOT (11.4%) and roughly one-fifth of SPCG-4, reflecting screen-detected vs clinically diagnosed pts
⚠️ No predefined AS protocol or surveillance criteria; sextant biopsies until 2009, prediagnostic MRI in only 21 pts
⚠️ Pre-2005 Gleason grading means some "low-risk" tumors would reclassify as intermediate today
⚠️ 'Failure' pools PSA relapse, HT initiation, metastasis and PC death; a low-value untreated PSA relapse counts the same as a death

verdict.rationale: Prospective single-strategy cohort within a screening RCT, no randomised AS vs immediate-treatment comparison; extends known low-mortality AS data from 15 to 25 yr.
verdict.audience: Screen-detected very-low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer, pre-MRI era…

studies.significance: 44 of 488 men reached RT off AS, and 18 failures were post-curative PSA relapse, so deferral shifts a share of pts into salvage rather than de novo definitive RT. Failure accrued steadily past 10 yr with no plateau, which argues for keeping the curative-intent RT window open decades out, not just through year 15.
studies.monday_clinic: For a man weighing AS for screen-detected intermediate-risk disease, these data put PC-specific survival at 85% at 24 yr and treatment-free survival at 30% at 19 yr against 99% and 55% for very-low-risk, informing how the surveillance conversation is framed; it does not speak to MRI-staged or high-risk pts, who were excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective cohort nested in the Göteborg-1 PSA screening RCT: of 1052 screen-detected PCs (1995-2014), 494 (47%) had AS as primary strategy and **488 were analysed**. No randomisation of AS against immediate treatment. Follow-up closed December 31, 2023; **median 18.0 yr** among men alive.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Very low risk 251 (51%), low 129 (26%), intermediate 108 (22%)**; high-risk excluded. Median age 66 yr (IQR 63-68), median PSA 4.1 ng/ml, median PSA density 0.12 ng/ml/cm³. Intermediate risk allowed **T1-2, Gleason 7, PSA <20**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: AS defined as no treatment within 6 mo of diagnosis, with **PSA every 6-12 mo** and rebiopsy on clinical or PSA progression. **No predefined protocol**: sextant biopsies to 2009, then 10-12 core; prediagnostic MRI in 21 pts.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: RT was a discontinuation route, not a randomised arm: **44 of 488** received radiotherapy off AS vs 141 radical prostatectomy and 47 hormonal treatment. Dose, fractionation and target volume are not reported. Post-RT relapse was defined as **nadir +2 ng/ml**, post-RP as **PSA ≥0.2**.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Kaplan-Meier treatment-free, failure-free, PC-specific and overall survival. **Failure** = noncurative PSA relapse, starting hormonal treatment, metastasis, or PC death, whichever came first. Curves truncated at 22 yr for treatment- and failure-free survival for want of men at risk.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **232 men discontinued AS, 81 failed, 14 died of PC.** The risk-group split is the read: PC-specific survival at 24 yr ran 99% very-low vs **85% intermediate**, and treatment-free survival at 19 yr 55% vs 30%.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Mortality tracks ProtecT (3.4%) and the Toronto cohort (5.7% at 15 yr), and sits above the <1% seen in PRIAS and PASS at 10 yr. It is roughly half PIVOT's 11.4% and a fifth of SPCG-4, which the authors attribute to screen-detected versus clinically diagnosed disease.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents screen-detected very-low- to intermediate-risk prostate cancer diagnosed without MRI or targeted biopsy. Does not represent contemporary MRI-staged AS cohorts, high-risk disease (excluded), or clinically detected tumors.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The failure composite is heterogeneous: an untreated PSA relapse held at low values for years counts alongside a PC death, inflating the 68% failure-free figure as a proxy for lost cure. Risk-group differences were **not formally tested** for significance, so the very-low vs intermediate gap is descriptive.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: Nearly half of all failures occurred **>10 yr after diagnosis**, tracking a lead time the authors put at 5-12 yr. The authors read this as no safe window for stopping surveillance rather than as a case against AS.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 44 of 488 men came to RT off AS and 18 failures were PSA relapse after curative treatment, so deferral moves a share of pts from de novo definitive RT into salvage. Failure accrued past 10 yr with no plateau, which keeps the curative-intent RT window open decades out.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: 44 men started hormonal treatment as their failure event, mostly for symptoms, and HT was the primary treatment in 8 of the 14 PC deaths. Gleason 6 vs 7 carried HR 3.12 (1.59-6.13) for failure, the strongest gate on who should not be watched.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Radical prostatectomy was the dominant exit from AS at 141 of 488, and PSA density doubling carried HR 1.78 (1.22-2.59) for failure. Sextant biopsy to 2009 means baseline undersampling drove some of that late crossover to surgery.

open_questions: Does MRI-based AS monitoring lower the late failure rate?
Can surveillance be safely de-intensified in very-low-risk men after 15 yr?
Is late salvage after AS curative as often as de novo treatment?

studies.name: POSEIDON
studies.tldr: IPD meta-analysis, 6057 pts: adding HT to PORT did not improve OS (HR 0·87, 95% CI 0·76–1·01, p=0·06).
details: 🔍 IPD meta-analysis of 6 randomised comparisons via MARCAP (RTOG 9601, GETUG-AFU 16, RADICALS x3, NRG/RTOG 0534); 5026 pts in the primary HT-vs-no-HT comparison, median f/u 9·0 yrs (IQR 7·2–10·7)
📊 10-yr OS 83·6% (81·8–85·4) PORT alone vs 84·3% (82·7–86·0) PORT+HT; absolute 0·7% at 10 yrs
📊 MFS improved with HT: HR 0·79 (95% CI 0·70–0·89), p<0·001; 10-yr MFS 74·1% vs 77·9%
⚠️ MFS gain did not clear the ICECaP surrogate threshold: upper 95% CI bound crossed HR 0·81 at every pre-PORT PSA value, so the MFS signal is not expected to translate into an OS benefit

details.text: 📊 OS by pre-PORT PSA stratum (HT added to PORT)

details: 📐 Categorical 4-strata PSA interaction was not significant (pinteraction=0·08); the binary >0·5 vs ≤0·5 ng/mL interaction was (pinteraction=0·02), confirmed in the two-stage within-trial model (p=0·03)
📊 Short-term HT (4–6 mo, 4 trials, n=3938): no OS benefit (HR 0·93, 0·77–1·11) but MFS improved (HR 0·82, 0·71–0·95)
📐 No significant interaction by HT duration (pinteraction=0·17); long-term-HT trials enrolled higher pre-PORT PSA and more adverse pathology
📊 Prolonging short-term to long-term HT (RADICALS, n=1523): OS HR 0·89 (0·68–1·16), p=0·37; MFS HR 0·76 (0·61–0·95), p=0·02

details.text: 📐 NNT to prevent one death at 10 yrs by pre-PORT PSA (any HT added)
subdetails: PSA 0·0–0·5 ng/mL: negative (point estimates numerically favoured PORT alone; imprecise)

details: ⚠️ Spline analysis: for long-term HT the upper 95% CI bound for OS HR crossed 1·0 only at PSA ≥1·6 ng/mL, far above the median 0·3 ng/mL seen in modern early salvage
⚠️ No multiplicity correction applied; the authors state secondary subgroup findings are hypothesis-generating
⚠️ Trials predate Decipher and PSMA PET; discussant Koontz notes applicability is limited to PET-negative biochemical recurrence
🔗 Contrast with the definitive-RT setting (MARCAP 2022, Lancet Oncol): ADT with intact-prostate RT improves OS, whereas the postoperative setting here does not

verdict.rationale: IPD meta-analysis of six randomised phase 3 trials, prespecified interaction analyses, 9-yr median f/u. Null OS contradicts routine HT with early salvage PORT.
verdict.audience: Post-prostatectomy biochemical recurrence, PET-negative, pre-PORT PSA ≤0·5 ng/mL

studies.significance: The decision this moves is HT omission at early salvage: at PSA ≤0·5 ng/mL the OS point estimates numerically favoured PORT alone (≤0·20: HR 1·14, 10-yr OS 89·9% vs 87·4%), and the MFS gain never cleared the ICECaP 0·81 threshold at any PSA. Where HT is warranted (PSA >0·5), 4–6 months matched 24 (prolongation OS HR 0·89, p=0·37).
studies.monday_clinic: In PET-negative post-prostatectomy biochemical recurrence salvaged at PSA ≤0·5 ng/mL, this questions routinely adding hormone therapy to prostate-bed radiotherapy; it does not extend to PET-positive nodal or metastatic recurrence, or to pre-PORT PSA above 0·5 ng/mL where a survival signal persisted.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: One-stage **individual patient data meta-analysis** (MARCAP consortium, PROSPERO CRD42019134376) of six randomised phase 3 comparisons of postoperative radiotherapy with or without hormone therapy, stratified by trial with univariable Cox models. **6057 patients**, median follow-up **9·0 years** (IQR 7·2–10·7); 5026 contributed to the primary comparison. Systematic search to Dec 15, 2024; single-centre trials and trials without metastasis or survival data excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Post-radical-prostatectomy men receiving prostate-bed radiotherapy for recurrent or adverse-feature disease. Median pre-PORT PSA **0·3 ng/mL** overall (0·3 in the short-term-HT trials, **0·5** in the long-term-HT trials); Gleason 7 in 67–68%, positive margins 58–60%, pT3a in ~35–38%. Race and ethnicity data unavailable.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: **Short-term hormone therapy 4–6 months** versus **long-term 24 months**. The short-term trials predominantly used GnRH agonists; RTOG 9601 used high-dose bicalutamide monotherapy, and RADICALS three-way used 24 months of GnRH-agonist ADT in 425 (86%) of 492 patients plus a 6-month group.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival.** Secondary: metastasis-free survival, event-free survival, biochemical recurrence (Fine–Gray). Prespecified interaction tests on pre-PORT PSA and hormone therapy duration, with 10-year restricted mean survival time and absolute Kaplan–Meier differences alongside the hazard ratios.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **No OS benefit overall (HR 0·87, 0·76–1·01, p=0·06)**, absolute 10-year gain 0·7%. MFS improved (HR 0·79, p<0·001) but the effect did not meet the ICECaP surrogate threshold at any PSA, so it cannot be read as an OS proxy.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: RTOG 9601 remains the only single trial showing an OS benefit, and it was **late salvage** at a PSA far above contemporary practice. The definitive-radiotherapy MARCAP analysis (Lancet Oncol 2022) found ADT improves OS with an intact prostate; the postoperative setting does not reproduce that.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PET-negative post-prostatectomy biochemical recurrence treated with prostate-bed radiotherapy at low pre-PORT PSA. Does not represent PET-positive nodal or metastatic recurrence, biomarker-selected (Decipher) patients, or pre-PORT PSA above 1·6 ng/mL where the long-term hormone therapy signal emerged.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Trial-level confounding by indication persists across strata: the long-term-HT comparison drew on only two trials with higher PSA and more adverse pathology, so its OS HR 0·79 is not cleanly separable from **case mix**. RTOG 9601 contributes bicalutamide monotherapy, not ADT, to that pooled long-term estimate, and enrollment predates PSMA PET staging.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The invited discussant framed the result as **either practice-changing or practice-supporting depending on current practice**, and restricted applicability to PET-negative recurrence. NRG GU006 (NCT03371719) tests whether PAM50 identifies a differential benefit from short-term hormone therapy with apalutamide added to PORT.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: At early salvage (PSA ≤0·5 ng/mL) the OS point estimates numerically favoured prostate-bed radiotherapy alone (≤0·20 ng/mL: HR 1·14, 10-yr OS 89·9% vs 87·4%), and the MFS gain never cleared the ICECaP 0·81 threshold. The omit-versus-add decision is the one that moves; where PSA exceeds 0·5, 4–6 months matched 24.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Duration, not intensity, is the read: prolonging 4–6 months to 24 gave no OS gain (HR 0·89, p=0·37) despite better MFS (HR 0·76, p=0·02). The long-term pooled estimate rests on two trials, one of which used bicalutamide monotherapy, so androgen-blockade class and duration are confounded with case mix.

papers.title: First Measurement: Proactive Immune Cell Sparing in Radiation Therapy
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Radiation Therapy (RT) can modulate the immune system and generate anti-tumor T cells. However, this anti-tumor-activity is countered by radiation-induced immunosuppression (RIIS). Clinical advantages of proactively sparing RT dose to immune rich organs have not previously been evaluated. Methods We conducted a phase II randomized trial from 2020 to 2023, enrolling 51 early-stage lung cancer patients treated with SBRT, to evaluate the effect of dose reduction to immune rich organs on RIIS. Two groups were: RIIS-optimized-treatment (lowering the dose to blood, bone-marrow and lymph-node-stations) and standard-treatment. All treatments followed national protocol guidelines. Peripheral blood was collected at baseline, immediately, 4-weeks and 6-months post-treatment. Results ALC changes from baseline immediately, 4-weeks and 6-months post-SBRT are: optimized-arm: -16%, -22%, -16%, standard-arm: -31%, -34%, -26%, leading to an overall-all-time-point improvement in ALC reduction in the optimized-arm compared to the standard-arm of 13.4 (5.3) % (95% CI, 2.8 to 24.0; p = 0.01). Central tumors had the largest improvement in ALC from baseline: optimized-arm: - 8%, -18%, -14%, standard-arm: -39%, -43%, -47%, leading to an overall-all-time-point improvement in ALC reduction in the optimized-arm compared to the standard-arm of 29.5 (9.6) % (95% CI, 10.1 to 48.9; p = 0.004). Grade 3 lymphopenia occurred in 15.4% of standard arm patients but was absent in the optimized arm. Additionally, 2.8 times more patients in the optimized arm experienced an ALC increase post-SBRT. Dose to organs such as the heart, great vessels, thoracic spine, and lymph nodes significantly correlated with RIIS. A trend towards increased Event-Free-Survival (two-year: 75.0% (SE = 10.8%) versus 59.8% (SE = 11.2%), p =0·10) and Overall Survival (two-year: 93.4% (SE=6.1%) versus 69.4% (SE=10.5%), p =0·14) was observed with optimized-planning compared to standard-planning in treatment naïve patients. Conclusion Reducing RT dose to immune rich organs significantly reduces RIIS compared to standard-of-care. This has implications in enhancing immune system mediated anti-tumor-activity. (Funded by National Cancer Institute and others. ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04273893 )
